Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset: production sprite PARTS for an existing tiny-pixel Godot RPG, not a character illustration.
Image 1 is the EXACT editable native sprite-parts atlas. Image 2 is the APPROVED assembled equipment design ("玄骸镇岳", male Lishi), use it only for armor materials, bone trim, orange ember, dark gray spiky hair and small bone crown.
Repaint ONLY the sprites already in image 1, IN THEIR EXACT SAME POSITIONS, bounding boxes, orientations, shapes, pose and scale. Output exactly the image 1 canvas 1024 by 1280, transparent background. Grid is four columns by five rows, each cell 256 square. Keep every blank cell entirely transparent. Do not move or center objects differently. This is an export texture consumed with fixed pixel regions.
Keep the face and exposed skin identical. Repaint the first spiky hair head with dark slate hair, orange streaks and tiny ivory crown from image 2. Repaint small torso/arm/leg pieces as black armor with simple ivory bone edge pixels and orange strips, retaining hand pixels and joints. Repaint the two large mace sprites black iron with ivory spikes and a small orange chevron core. Copy the approved color identities, but use the low resolution of image 1, not image 2 detail. Every native pixel in image 1 is enlarged exactly 3x; maintain that same coarse pixel grid, flat 2-3 shade materials. Do not draw whole people in cells: these are separated animation parts including some tiny hands and leg stubs. No extra objects, no shadows or glow outside silhouette, no antialiasing, no text or borders. Preserve alpha transparency and exact atlas alignment.
